<entry id="P01391">
<head-word>עָרַם</head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="P01305"> cmp. עָרָה I)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to peel off, strip; to make white, bright</italic>; v. 
<xref rid="P01325">עָרוּם</xref>, 
<xref rid="P01325">עָרוֹם.</xref></definition>
<notes /></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הֶעֱרִים</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to enlighten, inform</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Snh. V, beg. 22
<sup>c</sup>, sq. (ref. to בערמה, Ex. XXI, 14) שיַעֲרִימוּהוּ באיזו מיתה מת they (the forewarning witnesses) must keep him informed as to what kind of death penalty is expecting him; (Bab. ib. 80
<sup>b</sup> שיודיעוהו).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to plan, act deliberately</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Mekh. Mishp. s. 4 (ref. to בערמה, v. supra) להוציא … שאינן מַעֲרִימִין this is to exclude the deaf and dumb, the insane and the minor (who do not act with premeditation; להוציא מרפא … אינן מערימין to exclude the surgeon …, for although they acted with wilfulness (criminal negligence), they did not plan; Yalk. Ex. 325.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to act with subtlety, to get around a law by an artifice</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 65
<sup>b</sup> מערימין בדליקה in case of a conflagration on the Sabbath (when the rabbinical law allows the rescue of a certain number of clothes by putting them on) we may use an artifice (by laying off the clothes saved and going in again to save others); (oth. opin.) אין מערימין בדליקה you dare not &c. Ib. מהו שתַּעֲרִים וכ' dare a woman use an artifice &c., v. פָּרַף. Tosef. Bets. III, 2. Gen. R. s. 49 מה אתה מַעֲרִים על השבועה מבול וכ' why wilt thou cunningly evade thy own oath? destruction by water thou wilt not bring, but destruction by fire thou wilt? Yalk. ib. 83; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<binyan-form>אִתְעֲרִים, אִיעֲרִים</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>; 
<alternative>(also 
<italic>Af.</italic> אַעֲרִים)</alternative></definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to become prudent</italic>.</definition>
<notes>. Targ. Prov. XIX, 25.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be subtle, to deceive, pretend</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Macc. 23
<sup>b</sup> ודילמא אִיעֲרוּמֵי מִיעַרְמָא (not איערומא) might she not have been subtle enough (to discover Solomon’s motive)? Snh. 25
<sup>a</sup> דילמא איערומי קא מַעֲרִים perhaps he merely pretends (to be repentant)? B. Mets. 90
<sup>b</sup> הערמה … אַעֲרִימוּ עלייהו ויזדבנון a trick has been employed regarding them, use a trick against them (that did it), and let the oxen be sold (and not be used for ploughing).</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Af.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אַעֲרִים</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to use an artifice</italic>, v. supra.</definition>
<notes /></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="P01393">
<head-word>עָרְמָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> preced.) 
<italic>prudence, deliberation; subtlety</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Mekh. B’shall., Shir., s. 6 (ref. to נערמו, Ex. XV, 8, v. Targ. O. a. l.) הם אמרו הבה נתחכמה … נתת ע' למים they had said, Come, let us deal wisely with them (Ex. I, 10), thou, too, didst place wisdom in the water; (Yalk. Ex. 248 עַרְמוּמִית). Midr. Sam. ch. VII [read:] לפי מה שהיתה עָרְמָתוֹ של נחש כך היתה מכתו in accordance with the serpent’s subtlety was its punishment. Midr. Prov. ch. I. פתי הייתי ונתן בי הקב"ה ע' I was simple, and the Lord placed wisdom in me. Ib. מכמה שנים ואילך … להיות בו ע' from what age and onward is man expected to be deliberate?; Yalk. ib. 929; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="P01401">
<head-word>עָרַס</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (cmp. אָרַס) 
<italic>to connect, intertwine, braid</italic> &c.—Denom.</definition>
<notes> עָרִיס, עֲרִיסָה, עֶרֶס &c.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>עֵירֵס, עֵרֵס</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> (denom. of (denom. of עָרִיס) 
<italic>to form an arbor.</italic></definition>
<notes> Kil. IV, 7 אם עֵרְסָן מלמעלה if he connected them (the two rows of vines) above so as to form an arbor.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (denom. of עֲרִיסָה) 
<italic>to start dough</italic>, contrad. to לוש.</definition>
<notes> Y. Pes. III, 30
<sup>a</sup>; Y. Bets. I, 60
<sup>d</sup> top ע' לא אמר אלא לש וכ' the Boraitha does not say, ‘if one started dough’, but, ‘if one kneaded’; but if one started (on the eve of a Holy Day), this prohibition does not apply.—In gen. 
<italic>to knead, work in</italic> (cmp. עָרַךְ). Ber. 37
<sup>b</sup> בשעֵרְסָנ when he worked the crumbs again into a compact mass; Men. 75
<sup>b</sup> בשעירסן. Y. Ḥall. I, 57
<sup>b</sup>, v. עָסוּת.—Part. pass. מְעוֹרָס. Ib. וההן נשוך לאו כמע' הוא (not כמעירס) and that lump of dough made by pressing several pieces together (v. נָשַׁךְ),—is that not the same as if worked together?</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נֶעֱרַס, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְעָרֵס</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to become connected, compact</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sifré Num. 110 (ref. to ערסתכם, Num. XV, 20, sq.) משיִתְעָרֵס (it is subject to Ḥallah) from the time it has become a compact mass; Yalk. ib. 748 משתֵּעָרֵס.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="P01404">
<head-word>עֶרֶס</head-word>
<head-word>עַרְסָא</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>1) same.</definition>
<notes> ch. </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> same. Targ. O. Deut. III, 11. Targ. O. Ex. VII, 28. Targ. Y. II ib. XXI, 18; a. fr.—תשמיש (ד)ע' 
<italic>sexual connection</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. II ib. XIX, 15 (Y. I דעָרִיס). Targ. Y. Num. V, 13 דעריס; a. e.—Targ. II Sam. III, 31 
<italic>bier</italic>.—Snh. 20
<sup>a</sup>; Ned. 56
<sup>b</sup> ע' דגדא, v. גַּדָּא. Ib. ע' דצלא a bed with a leather mattress. Lam. R. to I, 1 ע' (רבתי) פחיתא a broken bedstead. B. Bath. 22
<sup>a</sup> לעַרְסֵיה וכ' waiting for the bier of R. A. Y. Kil. IX, 32
<sup>c</sup> bot.; Y. Keth. XII, 35
<sup>b</sup> יהבון עַרְסִי וכ' place my bier (coffin) at the sea-shore; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. עַרְסָן, עַרְסָתָא, עַרְסִין</plural-form>. Targ. Am. VI, 4 עַרְסַתְהוֹן ed. Lag. (oth. ed. עַרְסֵיהוֹן). Lam. R. l. c. אתקין … עַרְסָאתָא he prepared for them four beds. Lev. R. s. 5 (transl. מטות שן Am. l. c.) ע' דפיל ivory bedsteads. Y. Ber. III, 6
<sup>a</sup> top ע' קיסרייתא וכ' Cæsarean bedsteads which have holes for the girths; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (cmp. עָרִיס I) 
<italic>arcade along a row of buildings, sidewalk</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gitt. 6
<sup>a</sup> מצריך מע' לע' required identification of signatures on documents brought from one side of the street to the other. Y. Bets. I, 60
<sup>c</sup> bot. מע' לע' from one side of the street to the other (or from one couch to the other, v. טְעַן II).—
<plural-form>Pl. עַרְסָתָא</plural-form>. Erub. 26
<sup>a</sup> מערב … ע' ע' Ar. (Ms. M. ערסא ערסא; ed. עַרְסְיָיתָא, fr. עַרְסִיתָא) provided the whole town of M. with ‘Erubs (v. עֵירוּב), one for each row of connected houses.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>dish of the steel-yard, scales</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 60
<sup>a</sup>, v. עֲדָשָׁה.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> פאה 
<italic>to split, divide</italic>; v. Ges. H. Dict.
<sup>12</sup> s. v.) 
<italic>section, segment, corner</italic>.</definition>
<notes>—
<plural-form>Pl. פֵּאוֹת, פֵּי'</plural-form>. Erub. 51
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Num. XXXV, 5) פ' כתיבן the text speaks of corners (angular additions); ib. לזה אתה נותן פ' אין אתה נותן פ' וכ' for this purpose (the definition of suburbs) you allow corners to be included (i.e. square measurements), but you must not allow corners to those appointing a Sabbath center (שְׁבִיתָה), i.e. you must allow them to walk only within a circle the radius of which is two thousand cubits. Ib. 11
<sup>a</sup> בארבע פ' השדה Ar. (ed. פינות) 
<pgbrk id="pg1131" />in the four corners of the field; a. e.—Esp. </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> פְּאַת ראש 
<italic>the hair on the temples</italic>; פאת זקן 
<italic>the hair on the chin</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Macc. III, 5 המקיף פ' ראשו והמשחית פ' זקנו (v. Lev. XIX, 27) he who cuts off (shaves) the hair of his temples and destroys the hair of his chins; expl. ib. 20
<sup>b</sup> פאת ראשו סוף ראשו וכ' the 
<italic>peah</italic> of his head means cutting the tail-end of the hair of his head … making his temples as smooth as the spot behind the ear and as the forehead; פאת זקנו סוף זקנו וכ' the 
<italic>peah</italic> of his chin means the pointed ends of his chin &c., v. שִׁיבּוֹלֶת; Sifra K’dosh., Par. 3, ch. VI; a. e.—In gen. 
<italic>curls</italic>; פ' נכרית strange (false) curls, 
<italic>wig</italic>. Sabb. VI, 5. Naz. 28
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (פאת שדה) 
<italic>the corner of the field</italic>, the 
<italic>portion of the harvest left for the poor, peah</italic> (Lev. XIX, 9 sq.) Sifra K’dosh.</definition>
<notes>, Par. 1, ch. I פטור מן הלקט … והפ' is exempt from the duty of leaving for the poor the gleanings, the forgotten sheaf, and the corner. Ib. חייבים בפ' are subject to 
<italic>peah</italic>. Ib. אין פ' אלא מחמת הכילוי וכ' the title of 
<italic>peah</italic> comes only through the finishing (of the cutting of the field, i.e. if one left a plot uncut in the middle of a field, the poor cannot take it, before the field is entirely cut), and only when it has a name (has been designated by the owner as the poor man’s share), and the real 
<italic>peah</italic> is only that which is left at the end (i.e. he who has left a plot in the middle, must also leave a corner); ib. נתן בתחילה הרי זו פ' if he left a portion on beginning to cut or in the middle, it is 
<italic>peah</italic> (belongs to the poor, and is exempt from tithes &c.); Peah I, 3; a. v. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition> (transf.) 
<italic>braid, vines plaited together so as to form a cover or a partition</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Kil. IV, 5 אם היו קנים מדוקרנין עושה אותן פ' מלמעלה ומותר if forked reeds were standing there, he forms a plait above, and it is permitted (it forms a partition with regard to mixed seeds); Erub. 11
<sup>b</sup>. Y. Kil. IV, 29
<sup>b</sup> מציל משום פ' it saves (makes the place marked off by reeds a partitioned field) the same as a garland of vines. Ib. הדא פ' מה את וכ' what do you mean by that 
<italic>peah?</italic> do you mean overhead, or on the side? Ib. bot. הפ' אינה וכ' the ‘plait’ does not save (is not considered a partition), unless it is solidly joined on four sides. Ib. פ' מהו שתציל בסוכה do intertwined vines form a partition with regard to Succah (to be considered a wall)?; Y. Succ. I, 52
<sup>a</sup> bot. Erub. l. c. top פ' מותרת לענין כלאים וכ' (Ms. M. פ' קליעית קליעית, being a gloss to פ'; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) ‘braids’ form a partition with regard to mixed seeds, but not with regard to Sabbath laws; a. fr.—
<italic>Peah</italic>, name of a treatise of Mishnah, Tosefta and Talmud Y’rushalmi, of the Order of Z’raʿim.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
